question: What Settings localization contract should OpenClaw support for schema/uiHint-derived config labels and how should the two partial PRs be sequenced?
rationale: UI chrome can follow the existing t() locale pipeline, but schema-derived labels cross the config/schema and generated-locale boundary, and there are already two conflicting partial PRs that need a maintainer-owned direction.

options.title: Define one Settings i18n contract
options.body: Sponsor a single key/fallback design for Settings chrome plus schema labels, then ask contributors or ClawSweeper to rebase/replace the partial PRs against it.

options.title: Land only low-risk chrome slices
options.body: Accept toolbar or Quick Settings localization first and leave schema-derived labels as an explicit follow-up, preserving the current issue as the umbrella tracker.

options.title: Defer schema-label localization
options.body: Keep generated schema labels English for now and narrow this issue to fixed, non-schema Settings UI chrome only.

recommendation.title: Define one Settings i18n contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor a single key/fallback design for Settings chrome plus schema labels, then ask contributors or ClawSweeper to rebase/replace the partial PRs against it.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the most recent contributor to the Settings UI surface and can route the UX/API tradeoff across Settings, docs, and generated locale work.
